A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpaCeFormer and SpaCeFormer-3M. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality measurements, segmentation experiments, ablations, and qualitative/error analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a scene-size latency analysis in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The multi-view annotation pipeline, spatial-window/Morton backbone, RoPE-enhanced proposal-free decoder, training losses, and optimization procedure remain unchanged. Condensed descriptions and newly documented experimental settings do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Training retains ScanNet, ScanNet++, Matterport3D, and ARKitScenes; evaluation retains ScanNet20/200, ScanNet++, Replica, and Matterport3D. The new latency analysis profiles existing evaluation coverage rather than introducing a new task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes the EmbodiedSAM and OnlineAnySeg rows from the ScanNet200 class-agnostic comparison, although OnlineAnySeg remains numerically discussed in Section 5.1. Comparator membership in the other benchmark tables is retained.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported inference platform from a single H100 to a single GB200. The new Figure 9 profiles total and decoder-only latency over 160 scenes from five evaluation splits. Existing accuracy-evaluation protocols otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 9 examines how total and decoder latency scale with scene point count. Existing attention, positional-encoding, query-initialization, sampling, normalization, window-size, backbone, and error analyses are retained; relocated qualitative examples are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 9 introduces power-law fitting and R-squared reporting for latency scaling, with R-squared values of 0.87 for total latency and 0.97 for the decoder. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for segmentation accuracy.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 replace the uniform 0.14-second runtime with 0.22 seconds on Replica, 0.30 on ScanNet++, and 0.12 on ScanNet200 under changed hardware. Figure 9 adds scaling results, and Table 6 loses baseline result entries. Retained accuracy and ablation values are unchanged. Several speedup ratios remain unreconciled with the revised runtimes.

T1.justification: The appendix RoPE formulations, mathematical properties, window and overlap definitions, losses, and Muon derivations are retained with renumbering. Section 4.2 replaces explicit U-Net encoder/decoder equations with equivalent prose; the new latency fits are empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion refine the headline runtime claim from a uniform 0.14 seconds to benchmark-dependent timings spanning 0.12–0.30 seconds. The dataset and architectural contributions, interactive-inference claim, and headline segmentation-accuracy claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains near-linear decoder scaling versus sublinear total latency through changing backbone/decoder dominance. It adds specific future directions involving 2D-knowledge distillation and adaptive queries, plus a caption-bias qualification. The indoor-only evaluation and fixed-query limitations already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents FP16 autocast, inference batch size one, average scene point counts, and revised timing hardware. Sections 5.2 and A.11 newly specify the shared 512C ablation model, local batch size two, and H100 hardware while consolidating existing training details. Timing-estimation footnotes also become more explicit.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Gemma 3 technical-report citation and removes the OnlineAnySeg and EmbodiedSAM bibliography entries. Gemma 3 was already identified in v1's captioning appendix. The broader research positioning remains unchanged; other reference corrections concern bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Much of the introduction, related work, methods, experiments, and conclusion is substantially condensed and rewritten. Related-work subsections are merged, architecture equations become prose, ablation settings are consolidated, and numerous captions are shortened. Acknowledgements and an Impact Statement are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a compact first-page plot with revised supervision markers and legend, and new Figure 9 adds two latency plots. The former main-text Matterport3D Figure 10 moves to appendix Figure 15 and is enlarged. Numerous figures and tables are resized or relocated, including appendix Tables 14–15.

improvement.justification: The new latency analysis and clearer experimental disclosures strengthen the efficiency evidence, while extensive editing reduces repetition. However, revised runtimes introduce inconsistencies in central speed comparisons: Table 4 retains a 4,286× speedup after changing SpaCeFormer from 0.14 to 0.30 seconds, although 600/0.30 equals 2,000×. Table 6 also loses comparator rows. These gains and reporting regressions leave the net quality direction unclear.
